message.content:
For a homogeneous system to have a non-trivial solution, the determinant of its coefficient matrix must be zero.

The coefficient matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & k & -1\\
k & -1 & -1\\
1 & 1 & -k
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Compute its determinant:
\[
\det = 
1\cdot \det\begin{pmatrix}-1&-1\\1&-k\end{pmatrix}
-k\cdot \det\begin{pmatrix}k&-1\\1&-k\end{pmatrix}
+(-1)\cdot \det\begin{pmatrix}k&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Now,
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}-1&-1\\1&-k\end{pmatrix}=(-1)(-k)-(-1)(1)=k+1,
\]
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}k&-1\\1&-k\end{pmatrix}=k(-k)-(-1)(1)=-k^2+1,
\]
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}k&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}=k(1)-(-1)(1)=k+1.
\]

So
\[
\det = (k+1)-k(-k^2+1)-(k+1)
= k(k^2-1)
= k(k-1)(k+1).
\]

Set the determinant equal to zero:
\[
k(k-1)(k+1)=0.
\]
Thus
\[
k=-1,\ 0,\ 1.
\]

The answer is \(k=-1,0,1\).
